draft.briefing: Hey, you're on Munroe Island! It's a cluster of small islands where Ashtamudi Lake meets the Kallada river. Narrow canals run between the houses, so the best way around is by canoe.
draft.hungryLine: Munroe Island eats from the water: karimeen, prawns and crab.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Take a canoe through the narrow canals at sunrise, past coir makers and prawn farms.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the water at sunset and watch the canoes go home.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The island is named after Colonel John Munro, a British Resident of Travancore in the early 1800s.

legends.title: An island that's sinking
legends.body: Parts of Munroe Island are slowly sinking, and some homes now flood at high tide. Scientists are studying why.

legends.title: A lake with eight arms
legends.body: Ashtamudi means 'eight braids'. The lake spreads out in eight long arms.

tips.title: Canoe at sunrise.
tips.body: The light is golden and the canals are still.

tips.title: Agree the canoe price first.
tips.body: Ask how long the tour lasts.

story.title: Where river meets lake
story.body: The Kallada river and Ashtamudi Lake built up these low islands with silt.

story.title: Named by a Resident
story.body: Colonel John Munro, British Resident of Travancore, gave the islands to a church seminary. His name stayed.

story.title: Coir and fishing
story.body: Families here lived by coir making, fishing and farming prawns.

story.title: Rising water
story.body: Parts of the island began to sink, and life here started to change.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Canoe the canals at sunrise and eat fresh karimeen. Tell me what birds you saw.
